title: From illustrated city backgrounds to interactive 3D towns — my AI-assisted workflow for an Age of Exploration game
author: AlgondarAntillia
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/9glontogp7xh1.jpeg

https://i.redd.it/2lncjdgbp7xh1.png

Hi everyone! I’m a solo developer working on **Antillia**, an exploration and trading game on Steam set in the 15th-century Age of Exploration. I wanted to share how I’ve been using AI to help build its towns.

One of the challenges is the variety of architecture. Players visit ports across different cultural regions, so using the same European buildings everywhere wouldn’t really work.

Originally, I used illustrated backgrounds for the town interface, with small, medium, and large city variations. They worked as scenery, but I wanted the towns to become more interactive: highlighting individual buildings on mouseover, moving the camera toward a building when entering it, and showing some life in the streets.

That pushed me toward replacing the static backgrounds with 3D towns.

My workflow was:

1. **Generate building reference sheets with AI**, showing each building from four angles.
2. **Use those sheets as references for Astra**, which I asked to help model the buildings.
3. **Bring the resulting models into the game**, assemble the towns, and iterate on materials, lighting, camera framing, and interactions.

The four-angle sheets were modeling references—not a one-click image-to-3D conversion. The goal was to establish the building’s overall shape and architectural details before working on the model.

I’m aiming for a small, readable miniature-town look rather than photorealism. The towns still serve as an interface, so being able to recognize and select buildings matters as much as how they look.

I’ve attached one of the original city illustrations and a short capture of the current 3D towns. The water and people are animated in-game; the capture isn’t an AI-generated video.

There’s still plenty to refine, but this has been a useful way to tackle the amount of visual content needed for different regions as a solo developer.

Has anyone else used AI-generated multi-view references as an intermediate step for game assets? I’d be interested in how you handle consistency between the reference art and the finished models.
